questions.stem: In a factory, machines $A$, $B$ and $C$ are all producing metal rods of the same length. Machine $A$ produces 35% of the rods, machine $B$ produces 25% and the rest are produced by machine $C$. Of their production of rods, machines $A$, $B$ and $C$ produce 3%, 6% and 5% defective rods respectively.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a tree diagram to represent this information.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: M1: correct tree shape (3 branches then two from each, at least one probability attempted). A1: $A$, $B$ and $C$ and 0.35 and 0.25 labelled. A1: $D$ ($\times$3) and 0.03, 0.06, 0.05 labelled (may be implied by seeing $\mathrm{P}(A\cap D)$ etc at the ends).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the probability that a randomly selected rod is
(i) produced by machine $A$ and is defective,
(ii) is defective.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(i) M1: $\mathrm{P}(A\cap D) = 0.35\times 0.03$. A1: $= 0.0105$ or $\frac{21}{2000}$.
B1: $\mathrm{P}(C) = 0.4$ (anywhere)
(ii) M1: $\mathrm{P}(D) = \text{(i)} + 0.25\times 0.06 + (0.4\times 0.05)$. A1: $= 0.0455$ or $\frac{91}{2000}$.
[Correct answers only score full marks in each part]
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 1st M1 for 0.35x0.03. Allow for equivalent from their tree diagram.
- B1 for $\mathrm{P}(C) = 0.4$, can be in correct place on tree diagram or implied by 0.4x0.05 in $\mathrm{P}(D)$.
- 2nd M1 for all 3 cases attempted and some correct probabilities seen, including +. Can ft their tree.
- Condone poor use of notation if correct calculations seen. E.g. $\mathrm{P}(C\mid D)$ for $\mathrm{P}(C\cap D)$.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Given that a randomly selected rod is defective, find the probability that it was produced by machine $C$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathrm{P}(C|D) = \frac{\mathrm{P}(C\cap D)}{\mathrm{P}(D)}$, attempting correct ratio of probabilities. There must be an attempt to substitute some values in a correct formula. If no correct formula and ratio not correct ft score M0. Writing $\mathrm{P}(D|C)$ and attempting to find this is M0. Writing $\mathrm{P}(D|C)$ but calculating correct ratio - ignore notation and mark ratios.
A1ft: $= \frac{0.4\times 0.05}{\text{(ii)}}$, must have their $0.4\times 0.05$ divided by their (ii). If ratio is incorrect ft (0/3) unless correct formula seen and part of ratio is correct then M1.
A1: $= 0.43956...$ or $\frac{40}{91}$, awrt $0.44$ or awrt $0.440$

questions.stem:
A teacher recorded, to the nearest hour, the time spent watching television during a particular week by each child in a random sample. The times were summarised in a grouped frequency table and represented by a histogram.
One of the classes in the grouped frequency distribution was 20–29 and its associated frequency was 9. On the histogram the height of the rectangle representing that class was 3.6 cm and the width was 2 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Give a reason to support the use of a histogram to represent these data.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: B1: Time is a continuous variable or data is in a grouped frequency table

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Write down the underlying feature associated with each of the bars in a histogram.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: B1: Area is proportional to frequency or $A\propto f$ or $A=kf$. ("Area proportional to frequency density" or "Area = frequency" is B0)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Show that on this histogram each child was represented by $0.8\,\mathrm{cm}^2$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for a correct combination of any 2 of the 4 numbers: 3.6, 2, 0.8 and 9, e.g. $3.6\times 2$ or $\frac{3.6}{0.8}$ or $\frac{0.8}{2}$ etc BUT e.g. $\frac{3.6}{2}$ is M0: $3.6\times 2 = 0.8\times 9$
dM1: dependent on 1st M1 and for a correct combination of 3 numbers leading to 4th. May be in separate stages but must see all 4 numbers.
A1cso: 1 child represented by 0.8 - fully correct solution, both Ms scored, no false working seen and comment required.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The total area under the histogram was $24\,\mathrm{cm}^2$.
(d) Find the total number of children in the group.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: for $\frac{24}{0.8}$ seen or implied.
A1: (Total) $= \frac{24}{0.8} = 30$

questions.stem: The measure of intelligence, IQ, of a group of students is assumed to be Normally distributed with mean 100 and standard deviation 15.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that a student selected at random has an IQ less than 91.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $\mathrm{P}(X<91) = \mathrm{P}(Z<\frac{91-100}{15})$ attempt standardisation, $\pm\frac{(91-\mu)}{\sigma}$ or $\sigma^2$. Can use of 109 instead of 91. Use of 90.5 etc is M0.
A1: $= \mathrm{P}(Z<-0.6)$, awrt $-0.6$ (or $+0.6$ if using 109)
M1: $= 1-0.7257$, for $1-$probability from tables. Probability should be $>0.5$.
A1: $= 0.2743$, awrt $0.274$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The probability that a randomly selected student has an IQ of at least $100+k$ is 0.2090.
(b) Find, to the nearest integer, the value of $k$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $1-0.2090 = 0.7910$, for 0.791 seen or implied.
M1: $\mathrm{P}(X>100+k) = 0.2090$ or $\mathrm{P}(X<100+k) = 0.7910$ (may be implied), for a correct probability statement, but must use $X$ or $Z$ correctly. Shown on diagram is OK.
B1: Use of tables to get $z = 0.81$, for awrt 0.81 seen or implied by correct answer (calculator gives 0.80989...)
M1: $\frac{100+k-100}{15} = 0.81$ (ft their $z=0.81$, but must be $z$ not probability), for attempting to standardise e.g. $\frac{100+k-100}{15}$ or $\frac{k}{15}$. $\frac{X-100}{15}$ scores 2nd M0 until the $100+k$ is substituted to give $k$, but may imply 1st M1 if $k=112.15$ seen.
A1ft: for correct equation for $k$ (as written or better). Can be implied by $k=12.15$ (or better)
$k = 12$, A1 cao (2nd A1 for $k=12$ only)
Answers only: $k=112$ or 112.15 or better scores 3/6 (first 3 marks); $k=12.15$ or better (calculator gives 12.148438...) scores 5/6 (loses last A1 only); $k=12$ (no incorrect working seen) scores 6/6.
NB Using 0.7910 instead of 0.81 gives 11.865 which might be rounded to 12. This should score no more than B1M1B0M1A0A0.
